jobs.prompt: Build the baseline collector as a new module with tests (do not edit tools/swarm.mjs). Owner rule behind this work: no roadmap item is done until it is benchmarked against real data; every item ships a before and after table; the exit gate is better on its target metric and no regression above 10 percent on the others. Metrics (each reported as measured, estimated or missing, never invented): (1) ready_to_merged_ms per merged ticket; (2) billed_usd and list_usd per merged ticket split into workers, reviews and orchestrator (billed = paid lanes only, list = every job's reported or estimated cost); (3) first_try_pass_rate (jobs complete with zero retries), retries, flaky_failures; (4) owner_interruptions_per_day (decisions, approvals, blockers the owner resolved); (5) idle_slot_pct (slots free while tickets were ready); (6) dirty_tree_incidents, branch_switch_incidents, guard_false_positives; (7) orchestrator_tokens_per_merged_ticket. Create tools/bench-baseline.mjs (SPDX header, ES module) exporting async collectBaseline({root, project, since, until, now, readers}) returning {version: 1, project, window: {since, until}, generatedAt, metrics: {NAME: {value, unit, status: 'measured'|'estimated'|'missing', n, note}}, perTicket: [{id, readyToMergedMs, billedUsd, listUsd}], perDay: [{day, interruptions}]} computed from a project's own data with every reader injectable (default readers read the files): the run states under the swarm runs folder (jobs with startedAt, finishedAt, status, retries, agent, model, costUsd, costSource), the tickets ledger and its transition log (tools/tickets.mjs: readLedger and the tickets.log lines with at, event, id, from, to), the project journal and the orchestrator events (tools/journal.mjs, tools/orchestrator-events.mjs: pre, post, blocked and hand-built markers), the hand-build guard log (tools/handbuild.mjs LOG_FILE), the machine spend store (tools/spend.mjs spendDir and the daily file entries with usd, kind, tokens), the orchestrator usage numbers (tools/orchestrator-usage.mjs), and merged pull requests passed in by the caller as [{number, mergedAt, createdAt, title}] (so the module never calls the network). Rules: ready_to_merged_ms uses the first transition to ready and the matching merged pull request time when the ticket links one, else the transition to done (status estimated); billed uses only PAID_LANES from tools/spend.mjs, list uses every job; a metric whose source is absent is status missing with a note naming the source (never zero); first_try_pass_rate and retries come from job records; flaky_failures counts failures whose test name matches a flake list passed in (default: empty) or whose cause the field-export style classifier marks timing (status estimated); idle_slot_pct is estimated from wave records (tickets ready at start versus slots) when present, else missing; orchestrator tokens come from the usage module when readable, else missing. PRIVACY: the output contains only counts, durations, dollar amounts, ticket ids, run ids and day keys: no file paths, prompts, responses, branch names, commit messages or free text from tickets (assert with a canary string planted in fixtures), and a final scan with the repo security scan (tools/security-scan.mjs) fails the call with an error that names only the kind if anything secret-looking is present. Also export formatBaseline(baseline) returning a plain text table under 40 lines and writeBaseline({baseline, file}) writing the JSON atomically with mode 0600. Tests in tests/bench-baseline.test.mjs (node:test, strict assert, temp project fixtures built in the test, fake clock): every metric from a small fixture with known answers (3 merged tickets, one retried job, one paid-lane job, one free-lane job); missing sources give status missing; the canary never appears; billed excludes free lanes while list includes them; the day window filters; formatBaseline fits 40 lines; the file mode is 0600. Write only tools/bench-baseline.mjs and tests/bench-baseline.test.mjs.

Build the replay and compare harness as new modules with tests (do not edit tools/swarm.mjs). Owner rule behind this work: no roadmap item is done until it is benchmarked against real data; every item ships a before and after table; the exit gate is better on its target metric and no regression above 10 percent on the others. Metrics (each reported as measured, estimated or missing, never invented): (1) ready_to_merged_ms per merged ticket; (2) billed_usd and list_usd per merged ticket split into workers, reviews and orchestrator (billed = paid lanes only, list = every job's reported or estimated cost); (3) first_try_pass_rate (jobs complete with zero retries), retries, flaky_failures; (4) owner_interruptions_per_day (decisions, approvals, blockers the owner resolved); (5) idle_slot_pct (slots free while tickets were ready); (6) dirty_tree_incidents, branch_switch_incidents, guard_false_positives; (7) orchestrator_tokens_per_merged_ticket. Create tools/bench-replay.mjs and tools/bench-compare.mjs (SPDX headers, ES modules) and tests. Case format: a case is a JSON file evals/cases/NAME/case.json with {id, title, kind (build, test, docs, migration), prompt, files (repo-relative paths the ticket writes), context (paths), testCommand (argv array), acceptance (list of short lines), scrubbedFrom (a ticket id), sizeBytes}; validateCase(obj) returns plain error strings (required fields, argv array, no absolute paths, no path with .. segments, at most 8 files). scrubCase(raw) removes anything that could be customer data or a secret: it runs every string through tools/security-scan.mjs rules, drops emails and phone numbers and long random tokens, truncates the prompt to 4000 characters, replaces any absolute path with a repo-relative one or removes it, and returns {case, dropped: [{field, kind}]} (kinds only, never values). runReplay({cases, codeRoot, label, parallel, lanes, runner, now}) runs every case with parallel workers at most parallel at a time through the injected async runner(caseObj, {codeRoot, label}) returning {status: 'pass'|'fail'|'error', durationMs, billedUsd, listUsd, retries, tokens, flaky}; the default runner is a stub that throws (the real runner is wired later), so tests use fakes; it returns {label, parallel, startedAt, finishedAt, results: [...], metrics: {pass_rate, first_try_rate, median_ms, p90_ms, billed_usd_per_case, list_usd_per_case, retries_per_case, flaky_rate, throughput_per_min, idle_slot_pct}} where idle_slot_pct is the share of parallel slot time with no case running while cases were still queued, computed from the start and end times; a runner that throws marks that case error and the run continues; concurrency never exceeds parallel (assert it in a test with a fake runner that tracks in-flight count). runLoadSeries({cases, codeRoot, label, levels: [4, 8, 16], runner, now}) runs runReplay at each level and returns the three results plus a table of throughput, pass rate, idle slot percent and flake rate per level. compareReplays(before, after, {target, tolerance = 0.10}) returns {rows: [{metric, before, after, deltaPct, direction: 'better'|'worse'|'same', regression: boolean}], targetImproved: boolean, regressions: [metric], verdict: 'pass'|'fail', reason} where for each metric a lower or higher value is better as known (pass_rate, first_try_rate, throughput_per_min higher is better; median_ms, p90_ms, billed_usd_per_case, list_usd_per_case, retries_per_case, flaky_rate, idle_slot_pct lower is better), a regression is a worsening of more than the tolerance (a zero baseline counts a worsening above 0.01 absolute), the verdict is pass only when the target metric improved and there are no regressions; formatCompareTable(result) returns a plain text table (metric, before, after, change, verdict mark) under 30 lines plus a markdown form formatCompareMarkdown(result) for a PR body. Tests in tests/bench-replay.test.mjs and tests/bench-compare.test.mjs (fake runners, fake clock, no sleeps): case validation and scrubbing (canary email, phone, token and an absolute path never survive; dropped lists kinds only); concurrency bound respected at 4, 8 and 16; a throwing runner yields an error result and the run finishes; idle slot percent from a known schedule; load series produces three levels; compare: target improved with no regressions passes, a 12 percent regression on another metric fails, 9 percent passes, a zero baseline, a missing metric treated as not comparable and listed, table and markdown outputs fit their limits. Write only tools/bench-replay.mjs, tools/bench-compare.mjs, tests/bench-replay.test.mjs and tests/bench-compare.test.mjs.

Build the weekly scorecard and the swarm eval command core as new modules with tests (do not edit tools/swarm.mjs; a later job wires the dispatch). Owner rule behind this work: no roadmap item is done until it is benchmarked against real data; every item ships a before and after table; the exit gate is better on its target metric and no regression above 10 percent on the others. Metrics (each reported as measured, estimated or missing, never invented): (1) ready_to_merged_ms per merged ticket; (2) billed_usd and list_usd per merged ticket split into workers, reviews and orchestrator (billed = paid lanes only, list = every job's reported or estimated cost); (3) first_try_pass_rate (jobs complete with zero retries), retries, flaky_failures; (4) owner_interruptions_per_day (decisions, approvals, blockers the owner resolved); (5) idle_slot_pct (slots free while tickets were ready); (6) dirty_tree_incidents, branch_switch_incidents, guard_false_positives; (7) orchestrator_tokens_per_merged_ticket. Create tools/bench-scorecard.mjs (SPDX header, ES module): THRESHOLDS (frozen object per metric with green and amber limits and the direction, for example first_try_pass_rate green at or above 0.8 and amber at or above 0.6; ready_to_merged_ms green at or below 4 hours and amber at or below 12 hours; owner_interruptions_per_day green at or below 5 and amber at or below 15; idle_slot_pct green at or below 20 and amber at or below 40; flaky_failures green 0 and amber at most 2 per week; guard_false_positives green 0 and amber at most 3 per week; billed_usd per merged ticket green at or below 0.5 and amber at or below 2; orchestrator_tokens_per_merged_ticket green at or below 200000 and amber at or below 600000; the numbers are defaults the owner can override in a thresholds file), buildScorecard({baselines, replays, previous, now, thresholds}) returning {week: ISO week string, generatedAt, projects: [{project, metrics: [{name, value, status: 'measured'|'estimated'|'missing', grade: 'green'|'amber'|'red'|'unknown', trend: 'up'|'down'|'flat'|'new', previous}]}], overall: {green, amber, red, unknown}, headline: one plain sentence (for example 7 green, 2 amber, 1 red; first-try pass rate improved from 62 to 71 percent)}, where a missing metric is grade unknown (never green), trend compares with previous for the same project and metric using a 5 percent dead band, and formatScorecard(card) returns a plain text report under 40 lines plus scorecardForBoard(card) returning a small JSON for Swarm Watch (project, grade per metric, headline). Create tools/bench-commands.mjs (SPDX header, ES module) exporting parseEvalArgs(args) and evalCommand(args, {out, root, fs, now, deps}) for the subcommands: swarm eval baseline [--project NAME] [--since DATE] [--out FILE] (calls deps.collectBaseline and writes evals/baseline/NAME.json, printing the formatted table; marks which metrics are missing and what instrumentation would measure them), swarm eval replay --label NAME [--parallel N | --load] [--cases DIR] [--out FILE] (calls deps.runReplay or deps.runLoadSeries), swarm eval compare BEFORE.json AFTER.json --target METRIC [--tolerance 0.10] [--markdown] (calls compareReplays, prints the table or the markdown, exits with code 1 when the verdict is fail), swarm eval scorecard [--out FILE] (builds and writes the scorecard JSON and prints the text), with usage text and validation errors for unknown options and missing required arguments; all file access through the injected fs. Tests in tests/bench-scorecard.test.mjs and tests/bench-commands.mjs.test is not allowed: name the second test file tests/bench-commands.test.mjs (node:test, strict assert, fake deps, temp directories): grades at each threshold edge, missing metric is unknown not green, trend with the dead band, week string, headline sentence, board JSON has no free text, text report under 40 lines, every subcommand parses and calls the right dep, compare exits 1 on fail and 0 on pass, bad options print usage. Write only tools/bench-scorecard.mjs, tools/bench-commands.mjs, tests/bench-scorecard.test.mjs and tests/bench-commands.test.mjs.
